light_scene.intro_lead: Everything you see here is lit by the photometric data of {name}: a path tracer sends rays from the real intensity table into the scene. The picture starts grainy and sharpens as more rays arrive.
light_scene.intro_step1: Street, parking lot, facade or office. The luminaire is mounted at a typical height and aimed automatically.
light_scene.intro_step2: Photo shows what the eye sees. Illuminance paints lux values in colour. Grid places standard measurement points and reports averages and uniformity.
light_scene.intro_step3: Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom. Change mounting height, tilt, spacing and the number of luminaires in the panel on the left.
light_scene.hint_render: Drag to look around · scroll to zoom · switch to Illuminance to see lux values
light_scene.hint_isolux: Colour = illuminance in lux on every surface (scale in the panel) · lines every {step} lx
light_scene.hint_points: Points = measurement grids per EN 12464-1 / EN 13201-3 · the table shows average Em, minimum Emin and uniformity Uo
light_scene.desc_street: Two-lane road with cycle lane, sidewalks and a facade that catches spill light.
light_scene.desc_parking: Parking bays in the open, measured on the ground.
light_scene.desc_facade: Grazing or washing light on a building front.
light_scene.desc_office: Workplaces, measured on the 0.75 m desk plane.
light_scene.mode_render_desc: What the eye sees at night.
light_scene.mode_isolux_desc: Lux on every surface as colour, with isolux lines.
light_scene.mode_points_desc: Standard measurement points with Em, Emin and Uo per grid.
light_scene.stats_explain: Em = average, Emin = lowest point, Uo = Emin / Em (uniformity). Typical targets: roads Uo ≥ 0.4, office task areas Uo ≥ 0.6.
light_scene.aim_auto: Aim automatically (throw towards the road / facade)
light_scene.restart_tip: Start the accumulation over; rebuilds the GPU if it was lost
light_scene.nav_hint: Drag to orbit, right-drag or shift-drag to pan, wheel to zoom.
light_scene.samples_line: {s} / {smax} samples per pixel · {p} / {pmax} per point · key {key} lx
light_scene.cpu_note: The CPU runs the same transport in Rust at preview size: slow, but it works without WebGPU and cross-checks the grid values.
light_scene.no_webgpu: No WebGPU: tracing on the CPU at preview size
light_scene.desc_greenhouse: Glasshouse with two crop benches; values on the canopy in PPFD (µmol/m²/s) with the daily light integral.
light_scene.ppfd_from_spd: PPFD from the luminaire's spectrum: {f} µmol per lx·s
light_scene.ppfd_assumed: No spectrum in the file: PPFD assumes a white LED, {f} µmol per lx·s. Load an ATLA / TM-33 file or attach an SPD for the real factor.
light_scene.mel_values: {mean} lx mean · {min} lx at the darkest position (vertical illuminance at eye height, 1.2 m, × melanopic DER {der} of the luminaire's spectrum, CIE S 026)
light_scene.mel_day_ok: The daytime recommendation of at least 250 lx melanopic EDI is met at every eye position.
light_scene.mel_day_low: The daytime recommendation of at least 250 lx melanopic EDI is not met everywhere: {min} lx at the darkest position.
light_scene.mel_no_spd: No spectrum in the file, so no melanopic values. Vertical illuminance at eye height: {mean} lx mean, {min} lx minimum. Load a TM-33 / ATLA file or attach a spectrum.
light_scene.mel_note: Recommendations (Brown et al. 2022): by day at least 250 lx, in the evening at most 10 lx, at night at most 1 lx melanopic EDI at the eye. Electric light only; daylight adds to it.
light_scene.mel_card_edi: {lux} lx at the eye give {edi} lx melanopic EDI
light_scene.mel_card_need: 250 lx melanopic EDI need {lux} lx at the eye
light_scene.mel_card_estimate: Estimated from the colour temperature: this file has no spectrum.
light_scene.dli_explain: DLI = PPFD average × photoperiod, in mol/m²/day. Leafy greens want 12–17, fruiting crops 20–30.
light_scene.hint_ppfd: Colour = PPFD in µmol/m²/s on every surface (scale in the panel) · lines every {step}
light_scene.sensors_desc: Presence / motion detectors switch the luminaires: drag the person or a car into a detection area and the light comes on.
light_scene.sensor_none: No sensor files in the project
light_scene.control_nearest: Each luminaire with its nearest sensor
light_scene.move_hint: Drag a luminaire, the person, a car or a sensor on the picture.
light_scene.sensor_dim_off_note: Off: the sensors only detect, the luminaires stay at full output (as in the designer). Turn it on and move the person or a car to try the control.
light_scene.status_dim_off: Sensor control off · luminaires at full output
light_scene.status_no_area: This sensor detects nothing at {h} m.
light_scene.sensor_area: Detection area Ø {d} m at {h} m
light_scene.quality_desc_quick: Approximate preview: direct light plus an estimated even fill for the reflected light, lower resolution, no haze. Fast for moving things around; lux values are direct light only.
light_scene.quality_desc_balanced: One bounce of reflected light, every lamp at the first hit and one random lamp after it, medium resolution.
light_scene.quality_desc_high: Full path tracing at full resolution, every lamp at every bounce: the reference picture, slow on small GPUs.
light_scene.gpu_reset_note: The browser reset the GPU: quality lowered to Quick.
light_scene.gpu_gone_note: No GPU after the reset: tracing on the CPU. Reload the page to use the GPU again.
light_scene.auto_quick: Quick preview while the camera or an object moves
light_scene.denoise: Smooth the noise of the reflected light (picture only, not the lux values)
light_scene.desc_planned: From the {from}: {name}. Move luminaires, sensors and the person here to try alternatives; the plan itself stays as it is.
light_scene.open_in_light_scene_tip: Check this plan path traced: the room or area with its luminaires and sensors.
light_scene.planned_mixed_note: Several luminaire types in the plan: all are shown with the main luminaire for now.
light_scene.scene_saved: Saved in “{project}”; changes are saved automatically.
light_scene.scene_unsaved: Kept in this browser; save it to put it into the project file.
light_scene.em_mode_desc: Normal lighting off, emergency luminaires on at their emergency flux × maintenance factor. The picture starts dark, as at the moment the power fails, and adapts like an eye; points take direct light only, as the emergency lighting standards count it.
light_scene.em_marks: Show the plan markings (route, open area, equipment)
light_scene.em_marks_off: As a person escaping sees it: no markings.
light_scene.em_walk: Walk the route at eye height (1.6 m)
light_scene.em_check_note: Check in the Light scene: direct light, points every 0.5 m. The Interior designer’s results are the reference.
light_scene.em_off_hint: Switch emergency mode on to measure the route.
light_scene.em_adapted: 👁 Adapted: {stops} stops brighter than when the power failed. Kept below full adaptation, so emergency light still looks dimmer than normal light.
light_scene.moon_desc: Natural light for a date, time and place under a clear sky: by day the sun with its shadows and the daylit sky, at dusk the twilight sky, at night the moon and the stars; in the picture and in the lux values. Codes do not count it, emergency mode leaves it out.
light_scene.moon_readout: {phase} {pct} % · {alt}° up · {lx} lx on open ground (beam {beam} lx, sky {sky} lx)
light_scene.moon_below: The moon is below the horizon at this time.
light_scene.sun_readout: ☀️ Sun {alt}° up · {lx} lx on open ground (beam {beam} lx, sky {sky} lx)

sensor.use_loaded: View the loaded LDT as a sensor
sensor.not_applicable: Cone, beam angle, isolux and the other light-based views do not apply to sensors.
sensor.demo_note: Demo sensors are synthetic data, not products.
sensor.volume_ends: volume ends {d} m below the sensor
sensor.nothing_detected: Nothing is detected at this height. Lower the height or pick another sensor.
sensor.derived: Volume rebuilt from the measured heights ({h}); below the deepest height nothing is known.
sensor.recognised: {name} looks like a sensor LDT (ranges in metres, a mounting code in lines 33–42), so it opened here as a sensor.

colour_quality.title: Colour quality
colour_quality.cvg_text: Dashed circle = reference. Outside = more saturated, inside = duller.
colour_quality.cvg_note: Rg {rg} is an average over all hues. The shape shows where colours are pushed and pulled.
colour_quality.duv_title: Duv: distance to the black-body line
colour_quality.method: Calculated from the spectrum: ANSI/IES TM-30-20 (CIE 224:2017) and CIE 13.3.

sensor_compare.title: Compare sensors
sensor_compare.intro: Two detectors under the same conditions: the same mounting height, walking on the floor, seated presence on the workplane. Sensor LDT and SensXML can be mixed.
sensor_compare.need_two: Load at least two sensors: drop sensor files (sensor LDT, SensXML, GLDF) here or anywhere, or load the demo sensors.
sensor_compare.plan_note: A filled, B dashed; dashed line: the C-plane cut with the reach of both sensors.
sensor_compare.angular_note: Ranges in metres from the sensor to the edge of the detection volume (SensXML: rebuilt from the measured heights).
sensor_compare.quality_note: Δ = (B − A) / A. (i) interpolated, (e) extrapolated between / beyond the measured heights of a SensXML file.
sensor_compare.height_note: Diameter of the circle with the same area. A solid, B dashed; circles: measured heights of a SensXML file; a gap: not detected at that height.
sensor_compare.room_note: Fewest sensors on a regular grid that detect ≥ 95 % of the room (wall margin 0.5 m, both orientations tried); EN 15193-1 with one control group per sensor.
sensor_compare.link_note: Only demo sensors travel in a link; uploaded files stay in your browser.
sensor_compare.method: Both sensors are read under the same conditions: a sensor LDT is cut at mounting height − plane, a SensXML file is read at the mounting height. Data quality and test conditions of the two sources may differ.

sensors.intro: Place detectors in the room, see what they detect and estimate the energy saved with presence control (EN 15193-1).

sensors.mounting: Sensors in the ceiling at {h} m
sensors.auto_failed: No grid of up to {n} sensors reaches {pct} %; showing {n} sensors.
sensors.summary: {n} sensors · {a} m² floor area per sensor
sensors.hold_time: Lights off within 15 min of the last presence
sensors.hours_note: Assumed value; enter the hours of your building.
sensors.cond_group: Control group ≤ 30 m² ({a} m² per sensor)
sensors.not_credited: Not all conditions are met: counted as manual switching.
sensors.method: Coverage: the detection area of each sensor at the mounting height, cut at the floor (walking) and at the workplane (seated presence); wall margin excluded, walls stop detection. F_O from EN 15193-1 Annex E (F_OC by control type, F_A by space type; open plan interpolated between 10 and 30 m² per sensor), one control group per sensor, without daylight or constant-illuminance factors.

emergency.lum_room: The room's luminaires in emergency mode
emergency.spacing_note: At {h} m: escape route every {r} m, open area grid {g} m (from the luminaire's photometry).
emergency.route_hint: Click the points of the route's centre line; double-click or “Finish” ends it.
emergency.open_area_hint: Required above {limit} m²; the room has {a} m².

emergency.count: {n} emergency luminaires, {lm} lm each, at {h} m

emergency.floor_legend: Floor in emergency mode: direct light of the emergency luminaires, maintenance factor {mf}; min {min} lx, max {max} lx.
emergency.route_width_req: ≤ {w} m: split into strips or check as an open area
emergency.end_output: Output at the end of the duration (%)
emergency.end_output_hint: {std} allows lower values after {h} h: average {avg} lx, minimum {min} lx. Enter the output the luminaires still give then; constant-output LED emergency luminaires keep 100 %.
emergency.room_floor_hint: Checked over the whole floor; the room has {a} m².

en1838.label: EN 1838:2013 (Europe)
en1838.note: Escape routes up to 2 m wide: at least 1 lx on the centre line and 0.5 lx over the central half, Emax / Emin ≤ 40. Open areas over 60 m²: 0.5 lx without a 0.5 m border, ≤ 40. 5 lx vertical at fire equipment, first aid and call points; glare limits; Ra ≥ 40. Valid until 18 June 2027.

en1838-2024.label: EN 1838:2024 (Europe)
en1838-2024.note: Escape routes: at least 1 lx over the width less a strip of min(W / 4, 0.5 m) along each side (up to 2 m: the central half), Emax / Emin ≤ 40, at least two luminaires per route and open area. Open areas over 60 m² as before; 5 lx vertical also at door releases, escape plans and evacuation aids; glare limits; Ra ≥ 40.

bs5266.label: BS 5266-1:2025 (United Kingdom)
bs5266.note: The values of BS EN 1838:2024 (1 lx over the route less the edge strips, open areas 0.5 lx, 5 lx at equipment). Duration 3 h for sleeping accommodation, entertainment venues, phased evacuation or early re-occupation; 1 h only with immediate evacuation.

cte-sua4.label: CTE DB SUA 4 / REBT (Spain)
cte-sua4.note: Escape routes up to 2 m: 1 lx on the axis, 0.5 lx over the central half, Emax / Emin ≤ 40. Safety equipment and distribution boards: 5 lx horizontal. Anti-panic (REBT ITC-BT-28): 0.5 lx in the whole space up to 1 m, any size, no border. Zero reflectance, Ra ≥ 40, 1 h.

fr-erp.label: ERP, arrêté du 25 juin 1980 (France)
fr-erp.note: No lux values: evacuation luminaires at most 15 m apart along circulation routes, 45 lm or more each, two or more on routes over 15 m; ambient lighting in rooms for 100 people or more: 5 lm per m², neighbours at most 4 mounting heights apart, two or more per room. Illuminance is shown for information.

sp52.label: SP 52.13330.2016 (Russia)
sp52.note: Escape routes up to 2 m: 1 lx on the axis, 0.5 lx over half the width, Emin / Emax ≥ 1 : 40. 5 lx on the floor in front of every exit and at equipment and evacuation plans. Anti-panic over 60 m² (and 30 people or more): 0.5 lx without a 0.5 m border. Glare limits, Ra ≥ 40; 100 % within 10 s, 1 h.

nfpa101.label: NFPA 101 / IBC (United States)
nfpa101.note: Along the path of egress at floor level: average at least 1 fc (10.8 lx), at any point at least 0.1 fc (1.1 lx), max / min ≤ 40, over the route width and the room's floor. After 1.5 h the values may fall to 6.5 lx average and 0.65 lx minimum: enter the output then. Externally lit exit signs 5 fc (54 lx).

nbcc.label: NBC Canada 2020
nbcc.note: At floor or tread level: an average of at least 10 lx and a minimum of 1 lx over exits, public corridors, principal routes and the listed rooms; no uniformity ratio. Duration 30 min, 1 h (care, treatment, detention) or 2 h (high buildings).

nbr10898.label: ABNT NBR 10898 (Brazil)
nbr10898.note: Horizontal on the floor: at least 3 lx on flat areas, 5 lx where the level changes (stairs, ramps, obstacles), max / min ≤ 20 along the route. Duration at least 1 h.

gb55037.label: GB 55037-2022 (China)
gb55037.note: Minimum horizontal illuminance on the floor by place (GB 55037-2022 §10.1.10): stairs, front rooms and refuge spaces 10 lx, evacuation corridors and crowded places 3 lx, other places 1 lx; routes over the central half of their width, rooms over the whole floor, no uniformity ratio. Durations and switch-over times (GB 51309-2018) are not calculated.

jp-bsl.label: Building Standard Law (Japan)
jp-bsl.note: Direct light only: at least 2 lx on the floor at every point of the room and its escape corridors and stairs, corners included (fluorescent and LED sources; 1 lx for incandescent lamps). 30 min.

nbc-in.label: NBC India 2016
nbc-in.note: Escape routes up to 2 m: at least 10 lx on the centre line and 5 lx over half the width, no uniformity ratio; rooms checked at 5 lx. Duration 1.5 h, on within 5 s.

as2293.label: AS/NZS 2293.1:2018 (Australia)
as2293.note: Escape routes: at least 0.2 lx and an average of 0.5 lx on the floor, stairs 1 lx; measured away from the walls. From public summaries of the 2018 edition (the 2026 edition is not yet checked). 90 min in service.

nz-f6.label: NZBC F6/AS1 (New Zealand)
nz-f6.note: Direct illuminance on the floor: 1 lx in exitways and at changes of level, 0.2 lx everywhere else; points within 0.5 m of walls left out. 90 min.

spectrum_lab.title: Spectrum Lab
spectrum_lab.intro: One spectral trace → colour-over-angle, night vision (S/P), circadian (melanopic), mesopic road luminance, and a dark-sky report. The photons that build the LDT give you every metric because weighting happens at the detector, not at emission.
spectrum_lab.empty_hint: Pick a spectrum and press Trace to run the spectral Monte Carlo engine.
spectrum_lab.sky_tab_intro: Pick a place and a moment: the sun and moon update live, and the sky's light — daylight, twilight, moonlight — is traced onto a scene. Illuminance, colour and mesopic luminance come from the same Monte Carlo engine.
spectrum_lab.sky_empty_hint: Adjust the location and time, then press Trace to compute the sky's illuminance and colour.
spectrum_lab.globe_hint: Search a city or click the globe, then “Use this place”: its latitude, longitude and time zone are taken over.
spectrum_lab.moon_dist_close: close: {pct} % brighter than at mean distance
spectrum_lab.moon_dist_far: far: {pct} % dimmer than at mean distance
spectrum_lab.moon_times: Moonrise {rise} · moonset {set} · up to {max} lx at {at}
spectrum_lab.moon_hours: The moon alone gives 0.2 lx or more for {h2} h and 0.1 lx or more for {h1} h of the dark hours.
spectrum_lab.moon_dark: The moon stays below the horizon while it is dark.
spectrum_lab.moon_ref_note: Horizontal illuminance on open ground, clear sky. Reference lines: 0.2 lx = escape-route minimum of AS/NZS 2293 and NZBC F6 · 0.5 lx = EN 1838 open areas · 1 lx = EN 1838 escape routes · 2 lx = EN 13201 P6 average. Clouds, trees and buildings take much of it away.
spectrum_lab.moon_month_title: Moonlight over the next 30 nights (the most per night)
spectrum_lab.moon_month_hint: Click a night to show it above.
